name: Opel Air + Style Innsbruck 2016
description: First year at Olympiaworld rather than in the Bergisel stadium (Onboard's report places the arena in an open car park beside the Bergisel). Strong valley winds forced organisers to cancel the rounds after round two and to score the podium from the three highest combined round-two scores. Collective reports 2016 as the first year women competed at Innsbruck; Method Mag says the first women's field at Innsbruck was 2017. Shaun White announced during the event that the tour would expand to five stops. Exact dates not found in a source I opened.

name: Air + Style Innsbruck-Tirol 2017
description: Method Mag calls this the 34th edition and says it was the first year women competed in the Air + Style big air, with 30 men and 8 women plus 16 live music acts over two days. Tiroler Tageszeitung reports the Air+Style contest's history ended in 2017 in the Olympiaworld car park. Edition numbering here (34th) is inconsistent with Wikipedia's numbering (25th for Beijing 2013).

name: Air + Style Beijing 2017
description: Reported by Sport1 in February 2017; exact dates and venue not stated in the page I opened. [v0.2 flag: the row carries a February 2017 date but the German source dates the Beijing edition 25 November 2017. Unresolved.]

name: Air + Style Beijing 2019
description: Run as an FIS big air World Cup (FIS news item dated 15 December 2019). German Wikipedia calls the 2019 Beijing event the 25th and most recent edition of Air & Style. Exact dates and venue not confirmed in a page I opened.

name: Argentina Snowboard Tour 2012
description: Five events between May and August 2012: urban big airs in Buenos Aires (one of them invitational) plus stops at Cerro Chapelco, Cerro Bayo and Cerro Catedral. All but the invitational open to any rider regardless of nationality or level.

name: Argentina Snowboard Tour 2014
description: Third tour stop was the Snow Travel South America Snowboard Challenge slopestyle at La Hoya on 20 August 2014, the second time La Hoya hosted it and the final stop of the season for Brazilian riders. Other 2014 stops not listed in the source. Related Argentine events reported the same season: Rip Curl Grom Winter Search and the ALIVE and KICKING Rip Curl Pro (23 Aug) at Cerro Catedral, Bariloche, and the DC Slopestyle Pro at Cerro Chapelco (5 Aug).

name: Nine Knights & Nine Queens 2014
description: First edition to combine the men's and women's events, and the first with snowboarders on the roster.

name: Suzuki Nine Knights 2016
description: First Nine Knights at Watles; the edition built around the 'Perfect Hip' feature. A separate Nine Queens ran at Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis, Austria the same year.

name: Suzuki Nine Royals 2017
description: First official combined men's and women's, ski and snowboard event under the Nine Royals name.

name: Audi Nines 2018
description: First edition under the Audi Nines name after Audi became title sponsor and the event was rebranded.

name: Audi Snowboard Series 2013/14
description: More than 30 events across Switzerland in freestyle, boardercross and race. Named stops include a 3-Star World Snowboard Tour contest at Laax and European Cups at Davos, Lenzerheide and Lenk; the Swiss Championships in all three disciplines close the season, with the freestyle championships at Corvatsch on 11-12 April 2014.

name: 1st B4BC Snowboard + Music Festival
description: Inaugural festival, April 1996. Venue not stated in the source found.

name: 5th Annual Bomb Hole Cup
description: Day one banked slalom, day two open-jam park showdown. Held in April 2026; exact dates not stated on the resort page, which announces April 3-4, 2027 for the next edition.

name: 2009 Burton Canadian Open
description: Rated Swatch TTR 5Star. Mikkel Bang and Silvia Mittermueller won the slopestyle, reported by Onboard on 2009-02-09. Unresolved: the 2008/09 Burton Global Open Series calendar announced the Burton Canadian Open for 2008-12-01 to 2008-12-07 at the same venue, so either the edition moved to February 2009 or there were two runnings. Only one edition row is recorded here.

name: 1999 Burton European Open
description: Reported as the first Burton European Open, with the halfpipe at Axamer Lizum and the slopestyle at Seegrube in the Innsbruck area. Natasza Zurek won the halfpipe. Note that later edition numbering used by the organisers and the World Snowboard Federation (2011 = 12th annual, 2012 = 13th annual) counts the first edition as 2000, so the year of this first edition is disputed.

name: 2001 Burton European Open
description: The only year alpine snowboarders competed alongside the freestyle disciplines.

name: 2002 Burton European Open
description: Cooler's 2009 retrospective places the Burton European Open at Livigno, Italy for 2002-2004. Exact dates not sourced. Natasza Zurek won the halfpipe at Livigno in 2003.

name: 2014 Burton European Open
description: Presented by MINI. Halfpipe semi-finals on the LAAX superpipe 2014-01-16 with finals 2014-01-17; Iouri Podladtchikov and Ursina Haller won the halfpipe. Full event dates not sourced.

name: 2015 Burton European Open
description: Final Burton European Open. First event of the WST Pro Series. Slopestyle finals 2015-02-01, won by Stale Sandbech and Christy Prior; Iouri Podladtchikov and Kelly Clark won the halfpipe. Full event dates not sourced.

name: 2005 Burton New Zealand Open
description: Listed in the Scoop press-release archive; exact dates and disciplines not sourced.

name: 5th Burton New Zealand Open (2007)
description: Reported as the fifth annual edition, which puts the first edition in 2003. Competition ran from 2007-08-07; the closing date was not sourced.

name: Snowboarding at the 2007 Canada Winter Games
description: Games ran 23 February to 10 March 2007; snowboarding shared Mt Sima with alpine and freestyle skiing. First Canada Games held north of 60. Snowboard competition dates and disciplines not sourced.

name: Snowboarding at the 2015 Canada Winter Games
description: Games ran 12 February to 1 March 2015 in Prince George, BC, with snowboarding on the sport programme. Snowboard venue, dates and disciplines not sourced.

name: Snowboarding at the 2019 Canada Winter Games
description: Games ran 15 February to 3 March 2019. Snowboarding split between Canyon Ski Resort and WinSport's Canada Olympic Park near Calgary. Snowboard competition dates and disciplines not sourced.
venue_name: Canyon Ski Resort and WinSport Canada Olympic Park

name: Snowboarding at the 2023 Canada Winter Games
description: Games ran 18 February to 5 March 2023 in Prince Edward Island. Snowboarding shared the Brookvale venue with biathlon and cross-country skiing. Snowboard competition dates and disciplines not sourced.

name: 1987 European World Snowboarding Championships
description: Sources say only that 'Europeans host their own World Championships in January at Livigno, Italy and St. Moritz, Switzerland.' It is not clear from any source opened whether this was one championship split across two venues or two separate events. No dates, no format and no podium found.

name: freestyle.ch 2004
description: Admission was made payable from 2005 onward, partly in response to safety and crowd management.
catalog_status_note: Abandoned after the first day when the big air snow ramp collapsed. No injuries were reported.

name: Winter Gravity Games I (2000)
description: Only winter edition of the Gravity Games. Held in heavy snowfall. Snowboard superpipe, big air and boarder X plus skier X. No dates found in any source opened.

name: 4th Annual Holy Oly Revival
description: Announced by Lib Tech on 14 February 2007 as the fourth annual Holy Oly Revival. Exact contest dates not given in the source.

name: 7th Annual Holy Oly Revival
description: Covered by Snowboarder on 21 February 2010 as the 7th annual, and by the GNU and Lib Tech blogs on 24 February 2010. Exact contest dates not given in the sources.

name: 1993 ISF World Championships
description: First ISF World Championships. Snowboarder magazine's 1990s history timeline records Kevin Delaney (USA) and Michele Taggart (USA) as the combined title winners. No dates or event-by-event programme found. Terje Haakonsen is separately credited with ISF halfpipe world titles in 1993, 1995 and 1997, which suggests a biennial odd-year cycle, but no edition list has been located.

name: 1993 ISF Snowboard World Championships
description: First ISF world championships. Snowboarder/TransWorld 1990s timeline gives January 1993 at Ischgl, Austria and says Kevin Delaney and Michele Taggart won the combined titles; carvers.it repeats the same. German Wikipedia lists slalom, combined, halfpipe and giant slalom as the 1993 disciplines. Only the combined winners are recorded; no full podium found.

name: 1993 ISF World Championships
description: First official ISF Snowboard World Championships. Combined titles were awarded.

name: 42nd JSBA All Japan Snowboard Championships
description: 42nd edition; open-division champions listed on the JSBA historical champions page. Dates and venues not researched.

name: 30th Kaunertal Opening
description: 30th anniversary edition, run over three bluebird days on the glacier at 3,000m with the park spread across four locations. Separate pro contest categories for men and women, a Legends Invitational session, the Mega Testival, a Jib'n'Skate Jam and the KTO Music Festival. The mini-ramp returned after a 15-year absence. Sources give no exact competition dates; the World Snowboard Guide page is dated 13 October 2015.

name: 1981 King of the Mountain
description: Snowboarder/TransWorld timeline: 'Modern competitive snowboarding begins with a small contest held in April at Ski Cooper in Leadville, Colorado.' Wikipedia names the event 'King of the Mountain'. No podium found in any source opened. Some accounts list a slalom and a freestyle event; not confirmed.

name: LAAX OPEN 2017
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. The event joined the FIS Snowboard World Cup circuit in its second year. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2018
description: The LAAX Open Hall of Fame lists a snowboard halfpipe champion for 2018 but no snowboard slopestyle champion, so slopestyle appears not to have been awarded that year; the reason was not sourced. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2019
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2020
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2021
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2022
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2023
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Freeski slopestyle was added to the programme from 2023. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2024
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Freeski slopestyle was added to the programme from 2023. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2025
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Freeski slopestyle was added to the programme from 2023. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: LAAX OPEN 2026
description: Snowboard halfpipe and slopestyle. Freeski slopestyle was added to the programme from 2023. Confirmed held from the organiser's Hall of Fame listing; exact dates not sourced.

name: 1985 Legendary Banked Slalom
description: First edition. Sources disagree on the field size (14 riders per Wikipedia, 16 per Unofficial Networks) and on the date: Mount Baker Experience says February 1985, while Unofficial Networks says the race was deliberately scheduled for Super Bowl Sunday. Tom Sims won; Terry Kidwell 2nd, Ken Achenbach 3rd, Craig Kelly 4th per Mount Baker Experience. Course of roughly 500 feet with 15 gates.

name: 1991 Legendary Banked Slalom
description: Held year inferred: the organiser's Honor Roll covers 1985-2025 and the edition numbering chain (2016 = 30th, 2023 = 35th, 2025 = 36th) requires every year from 1985-2004, 2006-2014 and 2016 to have been run. One automated read of the Honor Roll flagged 1991 as possibly having no entries; not independently confirmed.

name: 2005 Legendary Banked Slalom
description: Listed by Cascadia Daily News and Wikipedia among the years the race did not run; the organiser's Honor Roll has no 2005 entries. Local Freshies notes the 2005 cancellation was followed by a season of roughly 800 inches of snowfall.

name: 2013 Legendary Banked Slalom
description: [v0.3 archive: LBS homepage announced February 8-9-10, 2013.] [v0.3 archive: LBS homepage announced February 8-9-10, 2013.]
catalog_status_note: [v0.3 QA: the dates previously recorded here were unsupported. The cited capture is the October 2012 homepage, which still advertises the 2012 dates, and it in fact resolves to a July 2012 capture. No archived page states the 2013 dates. Nulled rather than guessed.]

name: 2015 Legendary Banked Slalom
description: Intended as the 30th Legendary Banked Slalom. The 30th ran instead in February 2016. A substitute "29½ Banked Slalom" (one Saturday qualifying run, two Sunday finals runs) was announced for 21-22 March 2015 and cancelled on 18 March 2015.
catalog_status_note: The 30th Legendary Banked Slalom, scheduled for 2015, was postponed to 18-21 February 2016 for lack of snow. The organisers announced a scaled-down two-day substitute, the "29½ Banked Slalom", for 21-22 March 2015, and then cancelled that too in a 18 March update.

name: 2021 Legendary Banked Slalom
description: [v0.3 archive: Archive shows the 2021 dates were published (Feb 5-6-7, 2021) before the postponement notice replaced them.]
catalog_status_note: The 35th Legendary Banked Slalom was scheduled for 5-6-7 February 2021 and then postponed to 2022 because of COVID-19; the organisers' word was "postponed", not cancelled.

name: 2022 Legendary Banked Slalom
description: Cascadia Daily News describes a two-year COVID hiatus, with the race returning in 2023. [v0.3 archive: Archive shows the 2022 dates were published (Feb 11-12-13, 2022) before the "POSTPONED TO 2023" notice replaced them.]
catalog_status_note: The 35th Legendary Banked Slalom was rescheduled to 11-12-13 February 2022 and then postponed again, to 2023.

name: 1989 National Collegiate Championships
description: December 1989, so it belongs to the 1989-90 season. Single source; no format or podium found.

name: 1975 National Snurfing Championships
catalog_status_note: Cancelled for lack of snow (Michigan Snowboard Museum timeline).

name: 1976 National Snurfing Championships
description: Schlitz beer logo added to the competition bibs this year.

name: 1978 National Snurfing Championships
description: JEM Corp became an official sponsor and put up $1,000 in cash prizes; first place paid $400. Described by the museum as possibly the first paid snowboard/snurf event.

name: 1979 National Snurfing Championships
description: Michigan Snowboard Museum gives Blockhouse Hill as the venue and calls 1979 the final year there. Wikipedia's snowboarding article places the 1979 National Snurfing Championship at Muskegon State Park; other secondary accounts place a 1979 'World Snurfing Championship' at Pando near Grand Rapids. Jake Burton Carpenter entered with his own bindinged board and a separate open/modified division was created for him.

name: 1980 National Snurfing Championships
description: Series moved from Blockhouse Hill to Pando. 600-foot run; a slalom event was added alongside the downhill.

name: 1981 National Snurfing Championships
description: Michigan Snowboard Museum names the 1981 winners but does not name the venue.

name: 1983 National Snurfing Championships
catalog_status_note: Cancelled for lack of snow (Michigan Snowboard Museum timeline).

name: 1984 National Snurfing Championships
description: Museum timeline says the national snurfing championships ended after this period as snowboard technology outran the Snurfer; no edition is recorded for 1985.

name: 22nd Neil Edgeworth Memorial Banked Slalom
description: BC Snowboard's 2019 results index links a finals results PDF for the 22nd NEBS. Podiums not yet harvested.

name: 25th Neil Edgeworth Memorial Banked Slalom
description: 25th anniversary edition, organised with BC Snowboard. Dates not given in the source (article posted 1 April 2024).
venue_name: TELUS Park, Big White Ski Resort

name: Nescafe Open Champs 2010
description: Swatch TTR 4-Star halfpipe. The contest returned to Leysin after three seasons in Valais, with Nescafe back as title sponsor after previously backing it from 1994 to 2006. Return to Leysin after three seasons in Valais, and the return of Nescafé as title sponsor (a partner from 1994 to 2006). Announced as a Swatch TTR 4Star halfpipe competition. Exact dates not stated in the article I opened.

name: 20th NESCAFE Champs
description: 20th anniversary edition. Swatch TTR 4-Star, USD 50,000 prize purse and 850 TTR world ranking points to the winners. Slopestyle course combined kickers, a halfpipe and a wallride; warm spring-like conditions across the region but the course held up. The World Snowboard Guide report is dated 12 February 2011; exact competition dates were not given. Billed as the 20th anniversary of the Nescafé Champs Leysin and as the oldest snowboard event in Europe. Slopestyle course combining kickers, a halfpipe and a wallride. Winners took USD 50,000 and 850 Swatch TTR world ranking points, which corresponds to a 5Star rating.

name: 1987 North American Championships
description: Covered in the debut issue of TransWorld SNOWboarding (fall 1987) as the 'North American Championships in Banff, Canada'. No venue, dates, format or podium given.

name: Norwegian Snowboard Championships 2011
description: Halfpipe at Oslo Vinterpark on 27 March 2011; boardercross, big air and slopestyle at Trysil. Rated 3-Star TTR. Fields spanned ages 12 to 37. Silje Norendal, then 17, took two golds, two silvers and the King's Cup.

name: O'Neill Evolution 2006
description: Launch year. Inferred from World Snowboard Guide's statement that the event ran for eight years from its 2006 launch and had no 2014 edition; no per-year source opened for this edition.

name: O'Neill Evolution 2007
description: Inferred from World Snowboard Guide's 'eight years since its 2006 launch'; no per-year source opened.

name: O'Neill Evolution 2008
description: Inferred from World Snowboard Guide's 'eight years since its 2006 launch'; no per-year source opened.

name: O'Neill Evolution 2009
description: Inferred from World Snowboard Guide's 'eight years since its 2006 launch'; no per-year source opened. A worldsnowboarding.org event page for O'Neill Evolution 2009 exists in search indexes but now returns 404.

name: O'Neill Evolution 2012
description: Referenced by Whitelines alongside the 2013 edition; exact dates not found in a source I opened.

name: O'Neill Evolution 2014
description: Recorded as a not-held year rather than an edition.
catalog_status_note: No event held. O'Neill marketing director Claudio Curiger said the brand was working on a new strategy and that major events were 'no longer an issue for the time being'. O'Neill kept other Davos commitments such as park sponsorship and its flagship store.

name: 1989 OP Pro of Snowboarding
description: Single-source (Snowboarder/TransWorld 1980s timeline: 'OP Pro of Snowboarding held at June Mountain, California'). No dates, no podium. Disciplines inferred from Craig Kelly's published career timeline, which lists halfpipe and giant slalom results at a 1989 OP Pro - a rider biography, so not used for placings.

name: 1991 OP Wintersurf
description: February 1991. Won by professional surfer Gary Elkerton, which the magazine used to make the point that surfing is harder to pick up than snowboarding. Single source.

name: 1st PacWest Banked Slalom
description: Inaugural edition, created and organised by Marcel Dolak with Karter Riach, Olivia Cayley and volunteer diggers. Exact dates not given in the sources found.
venue_name: Summit East, The Summit at Snoqualmie

name: 2024 PacWest Banked Slalom
description: 290 riders in attendance. Exact dates not given in the source.
venue_name: Summit East, The Summit at Snoqualmie

name: Roxy Chicken Jam US 2008
description: Wikipedia records a projected purse of over USD 150,000 for the 2008 US event, one of the largest in women's snowboarding at the time. Exact dates not given.

name: 2011 Ride Shakedown
description: Series ran stops in Germany, the USA and Canada this year; Canadian dates not given in the source. SnowboardQuebec records Sebastien Toutant winning a third time.

name: 1985 Snoboard Shop North American Snowboarding Championships (first edition)
description: SnowboardQuebec's history page states Ken Achenbach's Snoboard Shop launched the North American Snowboarding Championships in Alberta in 1985 with a $20,000 purse, calling it the first snowboard event held in Canada, and says the series ended in 1988. Venue for 1985 is unconfirmed: the 1987 edition is sourced to Sunshine Village and later accounts describe an annual May long weekend contest there, but the one source naming a 1985 result places the event 'in Calgary'.

name: 1987 Snoboard Shop North American Championships
description: Held on the May long weekend with a $20,000 purse. A photograph of Dave Achenbach from this event ran on the cover of the first issue of TransWorld Snowboarding. Exact dates and the disciplines run were not sourced.

name: 1988 Snoboard Shop North American Snowboarding Championships
description: Norquay's own history says hosting the event put the resort on the cover of TransWorld Snowboarding. SnowboardQuebec's history records 1988 as the final year of the series.
catalog_status_note: Venue changed: Sunshine Village withdrew from hosting mid-season and Mt Norquay took the event on.

name: 1991 Victoria World Cup Japan
description: Snowboarder/TransWorld 1990s timeline: the Victoria World Cup Japan at Rusutsu, with over one million dollars spent, was 'the richest contest so far'. No dates, format or podium given. This is a single tour stop, not a full season row.

name: The Arctic Challenge 1999 (pilot)
description: Pilot project: Terje Haakonsen, Daniel Franck and Oakley invited 12 riders to Norway to test the concept. Halfpipe in Trysil, surfing and freeriding in Lofoten. Terje later described 2014 as '15 years since we did the pilot event'.

name: The Arctic Challenge 2000
description: First full competition: halfpipe, quarterpipe, surf, skate and freeride.

name: The Arctic Challenge 2001
description: Moved south because of weather: halfpipe at Hemsedal, quarterpipe at Holmenkollen in Oslo. Heikki Sorsa set a 9.3 m quarterpipe air record at this event.

name: The Arctic Challenge 2002
catalog_status_note: Cancelled after the sports marketing firm Sportsworld went bankrupt; Terje Haakonsen personally took on the financial obligations.

name: The Arctic Challenge 2004
description: Halfpipe and quarterpipe plus a music and lifestyle programme.

name: The Arctic Challenge 2006
description: First edition in Oslo.
catalog_status_note: Major weather delays; scaffolding had to be replaced before the event.

name: Oakley Arctic Challenge 2008
description: About 7,000 spectators in good weather.

name: The Arctic Challenge 2013
description: Main snowboard event on 9 March 2013, with a halfpipe competition (snowboard and freestyle ski) five days earlier; the volunteer call covered 6-13 March. Start date not stated explicitly.

name: 1st Toyota Big Air
description: Inaugural edition. Editions were normally held around 11 February.

name: 6th Toyota Big Air
description: Olympic year; the Japanese Wikipedia notes that in Olympic years the date shifted to late January or late February.

name: 10th Toyota Big Air
description: Olympic year.

name: 11th Toyota Big Air
description: The Makomanai open-air stadium carried the Sekisui Heim naming rights from 2007.

name: 14th Toyota Big Air
description: Olympic year.

name: 15th Toyota Big Air
description: Last edition held outdoors at Makomanai.

name: 16th Toyota Big Air
description: Moved indoors to the Sapporo Dome as a 'full model change', with a 36 m temporary in-run scaffold.

name: 2002/03 TTR Pro Snowboarding Series season
description: First TTR season: nine events worldwide with the Arctic Challenge as the final stop, each event awarding one TTR Medallion and an Arctic Challenge invite. No women's tour until 2005/06. Events: Nissan X-Trail Jam, Nokia Air & Style, O'Neill SB Jam, Burton European Open, Champs Open, Vans Triple Crown of Snowboarding, The Battle, Quiksilver Slopestyle Pro, US Open.

name: 2003/04 TTR Pro Snowboarding Series season
description: Same nine events as the previous season; the nine TTR medallion winners were invited to the Arctic Challenge, again the tour final.

name: 2004/05 TTR World Snowboard Tour season
description: Season edition rows use the calendar year the season ended. The Arctic Challenge's own 2005 site published the 2004/2005 TTR Tour standings, with Andy Finch as overall champion, which confirms the season ran.

name: 2005/06 TTR World Snowboard Tour season
description: Introduction of the 1-6Star tier system, the TTR ranking system, the first TTR website (ttrworldtour.com) and the official Women's Tour. 67 events in total. The TTR World Ranking list launched 5 December 2005 and the first-ever TTR World Tour Champions were crowned at the US Open.

name: 2006/07 TTR World Snowboard Tour season
description: First season with a dedicated women's tour, announced 24 October 2006. WSF described a provisional women's calendar of over 20 events offering more than 30 possible results, kicking off with the Burton Abominable Snow Jam at Mt Hood in July 2006 and ending at the Roxy Chicken Jam Finals in Park City, 22-25 March 2007. The Billabong Pro Junior in Australia and the Burton Australian Open were cancelled for poor snow.

name: 2007/08 Swatch TTR World Snowboard Tour season
description: Introduction of a $250,000 end-of-season prize purse. 176 results registered across four formats from events in 27 nations; 3,417 riders (2,706 men, 711 women) from 41 nations ranked.

name: 2008/09 Swatch TTR World Snowboard Tour season
description: First of Peetu Piiroinen's three consecutive men's overall titles, per Guinness World Records.

name: 2009/10 Swatch TTR World Snowboard Tour season
description: Second of Peetu Piiroinen's three consecutive men's overall titles; WSF reported he secured the Swatch TTR world title by winning the Oakley Arctic Challenge in March 2010.

name: 2010/11 Swatch TTR World Snowboard Tour season
description: Third of Peetu Piiroinen's three consecutive men's overall titles, per Guinness World Records.

name: 2011/12 World Snowboard Tour season
description: TTR's 10th anniversary season. Highlight was the inaugural World Snowboarding Championships at Oslo Vinterpark in February 2012, developed and owned by TTR and the World Snowboard Federation and run as a 6Star tour event - the first world championships organised by snowboarders since 1999. The Burton European Open was postponed to March, making WCS qualification difficult.

name: 2012/13 World Snowboard Tour season
description: First season under the new name. TTR announced on 2-4 July 2012 that the TTR World Tour would be called the World Snowboard Tour from the 2012/13 season; TTR president Reto Lamm said the tour then covered around 350 events across five continents. Headline events named in the announcement were Air & Style Beijing and Innsbruck, Burton European and US Open, O'Neill Evolution Davos and The Arctic Challenge Oslo.

name: 2013/14 World Snowboard Tour season
description: Season in which the six star tiers were replaced by four event categories: Regional, National, International and Elite.

name: 2014/15 World Snowboard Tour season
description: First season under the new tour concept agreed at the May 2014 General Assembly in Barcelona: six star tiers replaced by four categories (Regional, National, International, Elite), with the Elite events forming the WST Pro Series. Titles were awarded in slopestyle and halfpipe only, at the Burton US Open on 8 March 2015.

name: 2016/17 World Snowboard Tour season
description: TTR Pro Snowboarding restricted access to the World Snowboard Points List in January 2017 to force the snowboard industry to fund it. The merger with the WSF was announced 25 May 2017; from the 2017/18 season the merged organisation offered direct membership and the World Snowboard Tour brand ceased to exist.
catalog_status_note: Final season before the tour brand was retired.

name: 1983 National Snowboarding Championships
description: No lift access; competitors hiked the hill. Andy Coghlan won men's slalom and downhill. Several sources describe this, not 1982, as the first edition of what became the US Open, and Burton's own later edition numbering (2002 = 20th, 2009 = 27th, 2012 = 30th, 2020 = 38th) counts from 1983.

name: 1984 National Snowboarding Championships
description: Final year at Snow Valley. Andy Coghlan repeated in slalom and downhill.

name: 1985 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: First year at Stratton Mountain and the year the event was formally called the US Open Snowboarding Championships. Riders began wearing speed suits. Tom Sims won men's slalom; Andy Coghlan defended the downhill.

name: 1986 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Over 200 competitors in the pre-qualifiers. Andy Coghlan won slalom and downhill again.

name: 1987 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Craig Kelly won the men's slalom.

name: 1988 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Halfpipe debuted at the US Open and was immediately treated as the benchmark for competition pipes. Craig Kelly took the overall title. An ice storm preceded the event.

name: 1989 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Last year the downhill was run. Craig Kelly won the Overall title. [QA-corrected: the cited sources say halfpipe DEBUTED at the 1989 US Open and that Kelly took the Overall title; the earlier claim of a second consecutive halfpipe title was unsupported. The downhill discipline was uncited and has been removed.]

name: 1990 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Terje Haakonsen's US Open halfpipe debut. Craig Kelly won, against a field including Shaun Palmer and Jeff Brushie.

name: 1991 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Crowd and competitor numbers roughly doubled. Inverts ridden in competition for the first time. Janna Meyen won the women's halfpipe over Tina Basich.

name: 1992 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Terje Haakonsen won the men's halfpipe; Tricia Byrnes won the women's.

name: 1993 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Fresh snow and clear skies. Terje Haakonsen took a second consecutive halfpipe title on his new Burton pro model.

name: 1994 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Shannon Dunn and Todd Richards won the halfpipes. Terje Haakonsen sat out with an ankle injury.

name: 1995 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Big air debuted at the US Open. Terje Haakonsen won a third halfpipe title. Victoria Jealouse won the women's super-G, recorded here as discipline 'other' because super-G is not in the Linestry discipline vocabulary.

name: 1996 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Held in the season snowboarding's inclusion in the 1998 Nagano Olympics was announced. Peter Line and Cara-Beth Burnside won big air; Jimi Scott and Satu Jarvela won halfpipe.

name: 1997 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Reported crowd of over 10,000 for the halfpipe. Todd Richards edged Terje Haakonsen; Barrett Christy won the women's pipe.

name: 1998 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Remembered as 'the Year of the Mist' for heavy fog. Boardercross debuted. Rob Kingwill won the men's halfpipe; Nicola Thost, the 1998 Olympic champion, won the women's. Mike Michalchuk's back-to-back 1620s are cited by Burton as an early double-cork-era moment.

name: 1999 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Ross Powers won the men's halfpipe with McTwists and 900s; Nicola Thost won the women's for a second consecutive year.

name: 2000 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: First superpipe at the US Open, reported as roughly 300 feet long with 15-foot walls. Guillaume Morisset and Natasza Zurek won for Canada. Recorded as halfpipe; the pipe event was run as a superpipe from this year.

name: 2001 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Danny Kass won the men's halfpipe, narrowly over Vermont's Abe Teter. Natasza Zurek took a second consecutive women's title.

name: 2008 US Open Snowboarding Championships
description: Total prize purse reported at USD 471,500. Rated 6Star on the Swatch TTR World Snowboard Tour. Slopestyle finals ran 2008-03-21 (Shaun White and Kjersti Buaas) with halfpipe finals the following day; the event's start date was not sourced. Cheryl Maas and Tim Humphreys won big air.

name: 1990 USASA National Championships
description: Snowboarder/TransWorld 1990s timeline: February 1990 at Snow Valley, California; a severe snowstorm stranded competitors and USASA president Chuck Allen led the rescue. No podium found. City given as Running Springs, California (Snow Valley's town) - not confirmed in the sources opened. Not to be confused with Snow Valley, Vermont, which hosted the 1983 and 1984 National Snowboarding Championships.

name: Waengl Taengl 2013 (not held)
description: The crew said they would instead focus on youth development and new event formats.
catalog_status_note: The Aesthetiker announced a break from producing the event in 2013. Club president Steve Gruber: 'we felt we needed time to look at how we could step it up again to guarantee the next edition of the Waengl is kick arse, not an anti-climax.'

name: 1989 WestBeach Classic (first edition)
description: First edition. Sources disagree on venue and format: Whistler Blackcomb's own 60th anniversary timeline says the WestBeach Classic launched at Blackcomb in 1989 and that Ross Rebagliati won the halfpipe and landed the cover of TransWorld Snowboarding; photographer Dano Pendygrasse recalls the first event as a big air at Cypress Mountain. Venue left null pending a contemporaneous source.

name: 1997 WestBeach Invitational Big Air
description: Run inside the 1997 World Ski & Snowboard Festival (4-13 April 1997). Over 8,000 spectators at the base of Whistler Mountain. Exact contest date not sourced.

name: 2000 WestBeach Classic
description: Final edition. Moved out of the World Ski & Snowboard Festival to the May long weekend. Reported in 2001 by Pique Newsmagazine as the last running.

name: 2001 WestBeach Classic
description: The Masters Group organised both the WestBeach Classic and the World Snowboarding Championship.
catalog_status_note: Not held. WestBeach Sports redirected its funding to sponsor the World Snowboarding Championship instead; company president Steve Dewar told Pique the brand opportunity was 'too good to pass up'.

name: 2009-10 Winter Dew Tour, Toyota Championship: Northstar-at-Tahoe
description: Listed as the season finale of the 2009-10 Winter Dew Tour. No dates found; year assigned to 2010 on the assumption the finale followed the February Mount Snow stop, which is NOT sourced. See open_questions.

name: 2020 Winter Games NZ
description: Run in the new Obsidian format for New Zealand athletes only.

name: 2021 Winter Games NZ (cancelled)
catalog_status_note: Cancelled because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: 2022 Winter Games NZ
description: International athletes returned; 4 sports.

name: 2024 Winter Games NZ
description: Final edition. FIS World Cup events resumed; 4 sports. The Games were wound up on 23 January 2025.

name: Winter X Games II (1998)
description: Aspen Daily News gives January 1998; no exact dates found. Freeskiing, snowmobile SnoCross and skiboarding added to the overall programme. Discipline list is from a Snowboard Magazine results retrospective that tracked only halfpipe, slopestyle and big air; whether snowboarder X ran is unconfirmed.

name: Winter X Games III (1999)
description: Aspen Daily News gives January 1999; no exact dates found. Same caveat on the discipline list as 1998.

name: Winter X Games V (2001)
description: No exact dates found in any source opened. Moto X Big Air debuted at this edition.

name: Winter X Games VI (2002)
description: First Aspen edition; Buttermilk has hosted every year since. DATE CONFLICT, left null: the Wikipedia X Games article gives February 1-5, 2002 while the Aspen Daily News history gives January 17-20, 2002. Snowboard Magazine's retrospective suggests big air was not run for snowboard between 2002 and 2006, but this is unconfirmed, so disciplines are left null.

name: Winter X Games XXIV (2020)
description: DATE CONFLICT, left null: the Wikipedia X Games summary table gives January 23-26, 2020, the Winter X Games XXIV article gives 22-26 January 2020. Programme included a men's Rail Jam, a men's Knuckle Huck (recorded as 'other') and a Special Olympics Unified Snowboarding event.

name: Volkl World Rookie Fest 2008, Ischgl
description: Over 50 international competitors. Earliest Ischgl edition found in the WSF archive.

name: Völkl World Rookie Finals 2015
description: 3Star TTR event where the World Rookie Champion titles were awarded. Exact dates not given in the source.

name: World Rookie Snowboard Finals 2024
description: Confirmed only by a WSF news item dated 27 March 2024; venue and dates not established in this pass.

name: World Rookie Snowboard Finals 2025
description: Reported by WSF on 8 April 2025. Exact dates not established in this pass.

name: 2014/15 World Rookie Tour season
description: Eleven-stop season: South America Rookie Fest, Valle Nevado, Chile (Aug 2014); Australian Rookie Fest, Thredbo (Aug 2014); Iceripper Rookie Fest, Laax (Jan 2015); WSF World Rookie Fest, Livigno (Jan 2015); Bulgarian Rookie Fest, Pamporovo (Jan-Feb 2015); Transilvania Rookie Fest, Arena Platos, Romania (Feb 2015); Hellas Rookie Fest, Greece (Feb 2015); Trentino Rookie Fest, Monte Bondone (Feb-Mar 2015); Oslo Rookie Fest, Oslo Vinterpark (Feb-Mar 2015); Indy Park Rookie Fest, Nekoma, Japan (Mar 2015); and the 3Star Völkl World Rookie Finals, Ischgl (Apr 2015). Rookies were riders born 1997-1999, Groms 2000 and later. Events counted towards the TTR World Snowboard Tour.

name: 1996 World Ski & Snowboard Festival (inaugural)
description: Inaugural festival, directed by Doug Perry. Ten days, 22 competitions, about 1,500 athletes. Consolidated existing spring events including the WestBeach Classic, the Whistler Cup and the Couloir Ski Race Extreme, and added a snowboard museum exhibit and around a dozen bands. First joint marketing initiative between the two rival mountains and the Whistler Resort Association.
venue_name: Whistler Village, Whistler Mountain and Blackcomb Mountain

name: 2022 World Ski & Snowboard Festival
description: Returned after two cancelled years in a scaled-down weekend format under Gibbons Whistler ownership. Exact dates not sourced.

name: 2025 World Ski & Snowboard Festival
description: Whistler Blackcomb's own 60th anniversary timeline calls 2025 the festival's 30th anniversary; wssf.com calls 2026 the 30-year anniversary. Dates not sourced.

name: 1983 World Snowboarding Championships
description: The first snowboard halfpipe contest. Organised by Tom Sims with Mike Chantry; the pipe was pushed up with a snowcat and then dug out by hand. Riders on Jake Burton's East Coast team objected to counting halfpipe in the overall standings and reportedly threatened a boycott. No exact date found in any source opened; Sims' USPTO service-mark registration claims first use in commerce on 15 February 1983, which is the closest thing to a contemporaneous date. CONFLICT: a 2014 Snowboard Magazine piece on the Sims Retro World Championships refers to 'the 1982 2nd World Snowboard Championships in Soda Springs', implying a 1981 or 1982 first edition; every other source opened calls 1983 the inaugural year.

name: 1984 World Snowboarding Championships
description: Tahoe Quarterly states Terry Kidwell won the halfpipe at Soda Springs in 1984 and 1985; the Sierra Sun halfpipe history says Kidwell 'won the following two years' after Eddie Hargraves' 1983 win. No date, no full podium and no other disciplines confirmed.

name: 1985 World Snowboarding Championships
description: Second of Terry Kidwell's two Soda Springs halfpipe wins per Tahoe Quarterly. Note that Breckenridge's own history page claims Breckenridge 'hosts the first snowboard World Cup' in 1985 - a different event from this championship, and itself disputed (see open questions).

name: 1986 World Snowboarding Championships
description: First Breckenridge edition, March 1986, on a hand-dug halfpipe on Peak 9. Breckenridge had lifted its snowboarding ban in 1984, the first major Colorado resort to do so. Paul Alden persuaded Breckenridge management to accept the halfpipe as a legitimate competitive format; Swatch was a major sponsor and the event drew national media. Greg Stump filmed it for 'Maltese Flamingo' (1986). Terry Kidwell is reported to have won the halfpipe again in 1986 after the championships moved to Colorado (Tahoe Quarterly) - treated here as unconfirmed, no result row written. No full podium found in any source opened. Sources give only the month, not the days.

name: 1987 World Snowboarding Championships
description: DATE CONFLICT. The Snowboarder/TransWorld 1980s timeline and Paul Alden's obituaries put the second Breckenridge Worlds in March 1987 - specifically, NASBA was formed on 8 March 1987, 'the day after' the championships ended, which implies the event finished 7 March 1987. TransWorld's halfpipe history instead dates the 1987 Breckenridge World Championships to 2-5 April 1987 and calls its pipe (about 200 feet long with near-vertical six-foot walls) the best in snowboarding to that point. Dates left null. Jose Fernandes is reported to have won the giant slalom on an asymmetrical board (snowboarding8090.com) - not corroborated, no result row written. Craig Kelly's published timeline lists 'Swatch World Championships' results for 1987 and 1988, which is the strongest indication that the Breckenridge Worlds carried Swatch's name.

name: X-Trail Jam, January 2001
description: Launch edition. Wikipedia's results table lists two 2001 events, January and December, so the contest ran twice in the calendar year as it shifted to a December slot.

name: X-Trail Jam, December 2001
description: Second event of the 2001 calendar year; belongs to the 2001/02 season.

name: Nissan X-Trail Jam 2008
description: Last year in the Wikipedia results table. Later editions are referenced by Method Mag and WSF but were not confirmed year by year in this pass.
